description: L.A.B. New Ventures and Horizons is an engineering and educational simulation development team focused on space exploration mechanics. Our mission is to create interactive, scientifically grounded simulations for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, leveraging official open data from NASA (OSDR, RadLab, DONKI, Mars Trek) and partner agencies (CSA) to model autonomous outpost management, life support systems, and deep-space survival challenges on Mars.
summary:
Mission Ares is an educational game that turns real space science into clear, engaging missions for young explorers. Our team, New Horizons and Ventures, saw that complex scientific information can feel distant and difficult for children to understand. We aim to bridge that gap by translating real NASA and NOAA data into age-appropriate stories and choices—without changing the underlying facts.

Players guide a crew on Mars, responding to challenges such as dust storms and solar alerts. Their decisions affect resources and the crew’s well-being, helping them explore how choices can shape a mission. If a critical resource runs out, the mission must be aborted and the astronauts return early.

Our mission is to make space science more accessible and spark children’s curiosity. Our vision is to inspire young people from different backgrounds to explore science, with the long-term goal of bringing the experience to schools. Mission Ares values scientific accuracy, inclusion, collaboration, and nonviolence. The game’s outcomes are part of its simulation, while its scientific inspiration is connected to cited NASA and NOAA sources.
details:
Mission Ares is an educational game that helps children explore real space science through interactive Mars missions. Players guide a crew through challenges inspired by NASA and NOAA sources, including the 2018 Martian dust storm and a solar flare recorded in 2026. At each step, they choose how the crew should respond and see how those decisions affect mission resources and crew well-being.

The game turns complex scientific ideas into accessible, story-based choices for children ages 7–12. Its resource indicators and mission outcomes are simplified game mechanics—not measurements or predictions from NASA or NOAA. The project aims to spark curiosity about space science and make it more approachable for young learners.

We developed the browser-based game using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, and used the Inner AI platform during development. AI-assisted tools supported parts of the project’s development and content preparation; the team reviewed the materials and used cited sources to guide the scientific inspiration.

Our creative approach combines real scientific events, a fictional Mars crew, and decisions with visible consequences. We considered age-appropriate language, scientific fidelity, inclusion, collaboration, and nonviolent problem-solving.
